searchText: cc <@402080271563751435> Reference: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/595721451651465227/1562814032946139227 cc <@755590043632140352> moving the question to this channel <@755590043632140352>: `Hello, I'm reading an 8025 PR by @dapplion and have a couple of naive questions, not sure where's the right place to ask them. When verifying an envelope in an EL-less client, does the CL verify the consensus part of the envelope in full? I was wandering if there could be an edge case where the same EL payload commitment is included both in slot N, that slot comes empty, and then the next proposer picks the same block for N+1. There's RANDAO to save the day I believe for these types of edge cases, but still, from the pure EL perspective, payload can be valid if included either in N or N+1, as it only knows about its parent in N-1` The binding commitment that we currently use is the `new_payload_request_root` that includes the `parent_beacon_block_root` and as such a payload for slot N and N + 1 are not fungible. The `new_payload_requst_root` binding and execution proof inherits all verification properties of invoking the engine API `engine_newPaylaod` method. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/2344668a85b6263e117040afe7785fec9b6c55ca/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L984 If you would like a sneak peak at our future ambitions take a look at the`Execution Chain Proof` EIP - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12464. A recursive guest program that can determine EL chain validity from the weak subjectivity checkpoint to the head in a single proof (or k of n proofs). https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5725

When verifying an envelope in an EL-less client, does the CL verify the consensus part of the envelope in full? I was wandering if there could be an edge case where the same EL payload commitment is included both in slot N, that slot comes empty, and then the next proposer picks the same block for N+1. There's RANDAO to save the day I believe for these types of edge cases, but still, from the pure EL perspective, payload can be valid if included either in N or N+1, as it only knows about its parent in N-1`

excerpts.author: taulepton_
excerpts.content:
The binding commitment that we currently use is the `new_payload_request_root` that includes the `parent_beacon_block_root` and as such a payload for slot N and N + 1 are not fungible. The `new_payload_requst_root` binding and execution proof inherits all verification properties of invoking the engine API `engine_newPaylaod` method.

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/2344668a85b6263e117040afe7785fec9b6c55ca/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L984

excerpts.content: If you would like a sneak peak at our future ambitions take a look at the`Execution Chain Proof` EIP - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12464. A recursive guest program that can determine EL chain validity from the weak subjectivity checkpoint to the head in a single proof (or k of n proofs). https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5725
